native_source_candidate_only.motivation: Existing native orientation notes describe broad partly folded-looking green/brown blade bodies on f10r and f13r, but very different upper heads and lower root forms. f13r has a cluster of small pale dotted heads; f31r has clusters of small outlined round heads and a different large red root. This could guide one comparison of whether a distinctive component is reused across otherwise different compositions. The notes do not establish that any two components are actually the same depicted motif.

locators.f10r: Leaf bodies below the upper bent-stalk blue head; lower horizontal root with red oval ends.
locators.f13r: Broad middle/lower blade bodies; compact small-head cluster above; large red lower body.
locators.f31r: Top/right small round head clusters, left green forms, large red bent lower root.

native_source_candidate_only.required_native_question: Do at least two distinctively shaped component identities actually recur in a crossed arrangement across these whole drawings, as opposed to generic leaf/head categories or shared painting conventions? Preserve all three source images and negative comparisons; no species names or text-selected parts.
native_source_candidate_only.not_a_preregistered_candidate: These are cached review pointers only. The current reports support neither A+X/A+Y/B+X nor an independently measured counterfactual; do not call this a held combination.

distinction_from_prior_tasks: Same-whole Herbal↔pharma matching asked whether entire related plants have related text. GDT360 predicted broad inherited visual classes. The proposed part-reuse endpoint would instead require a concrete component identity retained while the rest of the drawing changes, and a second independent changed component, with whole-page text paired to the entire drawing. Branch labels are not a prerequisite. A generic rolled margin, color, blade category, head count, or repaired graph segmentation would not provide this distinction.
specific_minimum_missing: An independently recognizable repeated graphic component defined by more than the broad category root/leaf/head, on different complete plants, plus a complementary recurring component distinguishing their combinations. No exact written substitutions need be assumed before this visual discovery, but any later text model must face the crossed held configuration and suitable whole-page style rivals.
